resources.string: Runs your scripts when the IDE opens or closes a project, opens, saves or closes a file, or builds. Off until you turn it on.
Name an executable script after a hook, or put several in <hook>.d/. Scripts in actions/ appear as Run <name> on a file\'s menu. In the Terminal this folder is ~/.config/codeonthego/hooks.

resources.string: Stop a script after this many seconds
Enter a whole number of seconds from %1$d to %2$d. The timeout stays at %3$d until you do.

Scripts in a project\'s .codeonthego/hooks folder run only after you read and trust them in the Hooks tab, because a script can arrive with a project: a cloned repository, or an AI agent\'s edit. Only plain scripts can be trusted: printable ASCII and newlines, no tabs, no line over 100 characters or ending in a space, at most 64 KB. They need no executable bit.
Shell Hooks is off. Turn it on in Preferences, Shell Hooks.

Can\'t be reviewed: %1$s. A project script can be trusted only if it is plain: printable ASCII and newlines, no tabs or carriage returns, no line over 100 characters or ending in a space, at most 64 KB, and a name of letters, digits, \'.\', \'_\', \'-\' and \'/\'. Anything else could look different here from how it runs, so it never runs.
